BUTCH.text: Thank you for treating the facts as facts.

LEV.text: It is the least glamorous part of the job.

CONDUCTOR.text: Echo City. Passengers leaving the train, please step onto the platform. Keep the doorway clear.

TOMA.text: Public hall is open. What business are you bringing inside?

NIKA.text: Sava authorized the search. I can show you timestamps, not conclusions.

EDA.text: If this is about the smell, I already called Sanitation. They sent me a complaint form instead of a cleaner.

OLEK.text: I carried two sealed cans. I did not open them.

PETAR.text: I did not see a message. I worked from the access chamber below the paving.

HANA.text: That is generally how the book works.

SELINE.text: Rada says this is a celebration. It is really an excuse to keep me from going back for another shift.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: I have a claim card, not a ticket. 1978-0412. The orchard case is still on board.
items.say: I have a claim card, not a ticket. Nineteen seventy-eight, oh four one two. The orchard case is still on board.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: She said she would leave another mark where she could. The last one pointed here.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Fresh lamp oil, poured by hand along every joint, over stone somebody cleaned first.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Yesterday's ticket forty-three. Both of them.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Sava keeps the issue records. Every search at that terminal goes out under his stamp.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: One seat, one claim, two tickets. The archive printed her twice.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: The duplicate is a clerical ghost. The oil is not: it was bought on the same seat. Eda's stall, west past the clock.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: That stub on your ledger is seat forty-three. Did she stay here?

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Another mark. She said she would leave one where she could.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: This afternoon's oil line. It was never a spill. It was the first row.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: It lit on the bell. As if she knew the minute I would kneel here.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Keep moving. The night service calls at seven.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: No name on the laundry ticket?

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Cold as the archive stacks. I will keep it out of the municipal ledger.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Something blue catches in the cold ashes, under a coat someone left by the fire.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Then I will not go alone.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: Mara.

items.speaker: BUTCH
items.text: One step ahead. Always one step.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: Keep that card out.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: That claim number went through our station reader yesterday. Twice.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: Two tickets forty-three, one seat, both valid. And someone poured a line of lamp oil into the paving. We start with the oil.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: Oil is bought, and yesterday someone paid for this on seat forty-three. The ministry is northeast, past the fountain. Toma keeps the door.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: Lay both on the public table. We look at them before anyone tells us what they mean.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: Two true things, filed as two people.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: That crossing has a scanner. It flags anyone who crosses alone. Walk beside Olek, in step, and it reads you as one party.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: The service joint at the south edge of the clock paving feeds the old fire letters, two rows in the grooves. The light is going; we should see it before dark.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: Sleep. I will find you before the first train.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: The platform is past the square, where the rails come in. The night service will not wait for either of us.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: The platform scanner reads parties, not heads. Alone, it holds you at the line.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: This way. The tall stone front on the east lane. Toma keeps the door.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: West, past the clock. Eda sells lamp oil under the blue canvas.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: The service joint is by the clock, at the south edge of the square.

items.speaker: LEV
items.text: The Copper Heron. Past the ministry lane, at the east end of the street.

items.speaker: CONDUCTOR
items.text: The night service calls back at seven tomorrow. Be on the platform.

items.speaker: TOMA
items.text: Nika runs the ticket terminal. The window on the right.

items.speaker: NIKA
items.text: A market sale at fourteen twelve. Two cans of lamp oil, stamped with the seat number. Eda's stall.

items.speaker: NIKA
items.text: The first forty-three was issued to VELEZ, M. The second printed on the same seat, so the terminal filed it as a duplicate.
items.say: The first forty-three was issued to Velez, M. The second printed on the same seat, so the terminal filed it as a duplicate.

items.speaker: NIKA
items.text: Terminals cut long surnames on duplicates. Two letters, then NN for no name on file. My note is with the prints.
items.say: Terminals cut long surnames on duplicates. Two letters, then N N for no name on file. My note is with the prints.

items.speaker: EDA
items.text: A good coat, a rose scarf, a ticket in her glove. She kept her face to the street the whole time.

items.speaker: EDA
items.text: Olek carried the two cans for her, the woman in the rose scarf. He is taking the cart through the ward crossing now.

items.speaker: OLEK
items.text: She said leave them by the clock paving, at the service joint. She walked ahead the whole way.

items.speaker: OLEK
items.text: I never saw her face. Only the scarf.

items.speaker: OLEK
items.text: That is the trick of it. Two people in step and the machine counts one party.

items.speaker: PETAR
items.text: Order C-441. An unregistered branch under the clock paving was losing pressure, so I cut it.
items.say: Order C four four one. An unregistered branch under the clock paving was losing pressure, so I cut it.

items.speaker: PETAR
items.text: If you want warmth first, the laundry crew keep a fire by the west wall at dusk. Seline has been showing everyone something she found.

items.speaker: HANA
items.text: No. Not once. She kept the scarf up and her back to the lamp. I remember thinking she was very good at it.

items.speaker: SELINE
items.text: You inspect strange things, do you not? I found this sewn into an unclaimed coat lining.

items.speaker: SELINE
items.text: No ticket. The stone hums whenever the evening tram passes. I would rather you take it.
